matt: Quick perf note — ran fused-attn (QKV compact pack + bias/rope epilogue) across paged-KV profile for long-context chat (L=8192). Observed a "thermostat" curve: p50 stable but p99 jumps nonlinearly as batch grows.

sasha: env + build? drop the numbers pls.

matt: g5x2, CUDA 12.2, FA variant=flash2_opt, kernel tag=perf/flash2-epqv1. Batch sweep 1..64 with paged-KV ON. Seq=8192. Results below.

```
batch:   p50(ms)  p95(ms)  p99(ms)
1:       22       40       55
4:       25       45       120
8:       30       60       240
16:      48       120      650
32:      95       220      1300
64:      180      400      2700
```

anjali: whoa, p99 growth is super nonlinear. smells like paged-KV eviction / memory thrash. Did you capture L2 / register pressure?

matt: yes — nvprof + nsight show big L2 miss spikes starting at batch>=8, and epilogue kernels stall waiting on prefetched pages. Prefetch buffer occupancy also spikes.

kevin: is this regression only with fused epilogue? what about splitting bias+rope from the epilogue?

matt: tried split epilogue (bias add -> rope -> softmax postproc as separate kernels). p99 improves ~30% for batch 16/32 but p50 slightly worse. So fusion yields throughput but amplifies tails under paged-KV contention.

raja: idea: kernel-chooser should be "paged-KV aware". thermostat heuristic: cap effective batch when page-fault rate or L2-miss-rate crosses a threshold. Choose a smaller, lower-pressure kernel to guarantee SLO.

matt: exactly. Proposed short heuristic: sample 1s of live traffic, compute page-faults/sec and L2-misses-per-token, then pick batch size s.t. projected p99 < SLO (e.g., 500ms). Add a conservative prefetch-window reduction knob when page-faults spike.

jen: can you try coalesced prefetch + disable speculative prefetch? also instrument KV eviction count per request (add as metric).

matt: on it. also observed that FA2 (flash2_opt) uses higher register pressure in epilogue leading to register spills when combined with prefetch buffers. FA1 had lower regs and avoided worst p99 spikes but had lower peak throughput. So fallback-to-FA1 might be a viable policy for tail-sensitive workloads.

ops-bot: nightly-bench-run finished: http://ci/bench/2491234567 (artifacts + nvprof captures).

sasha: matt pls drop a tiny reproducer in /eng-runtime/perf-playgrounds and ping me + attach nvprof timeline.

matt: added gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/perf-repro-2491234567 with run.sh, sample config, nvprof flags and kernel build tag. Reproducer reproduces p99 spikes within ~30s.

anjali: long-term: expose per-model kernel selection policy, e.g. "pagedKvAware": true. Runtime can then autoscale batching vs throughput. Also add telemetry: token-level page-fault rate, eviction-rate, epilogue-wait-ms.

kevin: +1. Another immediate mitigation: add chooser rule: if page-fault-rate > X OR L2-miss-per-token > Y then: prefer FA1 or reduce batch by factor 2.

raja: we should also add a canary test in Dedicated that simulates long-context paged-KV traffic to catch regressions in FA variants.

matt: will open PR with: (1) knob for "pagedKvAware" kernel selection, (2) fallback policy FA2->FA1, (3) token-level page-fault telemetry to Console.

jen: thanks — let's sync tomorrow 10:00 to review the PR and the nvprof timelines. :thumbsup:

matt: excellent. tagging @sasha @anjali for follow-up.
